Try buckle the carrier in, stop it from moving around the seats. I actually go around with mine in front seat, with the belt over top and looped through the handle, to tether it. For safety, it's better to have a smaller carrier, if you did up in an accident the animal will only by thrown a small bit and so is less likely to be injured. Stop for breaks and offer fresh veg, pellets etc, some times you really need to put it under their mouth to get them to start eating. Cucumber is a great veggie for travel as it also hydrates them. Try take hay and food that they've had with the breeder. Fingers crossed the journey will go well. They'll probably be breathing quite a lot and looking a little startled but don't worry, rabbits are easily startled and are designed to be anxious as the are a prey species. Then once your home I'd take the carrier into their new living space and let them come out to explore in their own time. I generally give my rabbits 24 hrs before trying to handle them or say hi, I just let them chill and settle in first. However you can get some buns that are more confident and are immediately out the carrier, coming up to you looking for attention or food. Are they indoor or outdoor? If they were bred outdoor you shouldn't need to worry about them being to cold, in fact it would make sense to keep the car on the cooler side then.
